physicalEvidence.status: Actual learned onboard aerial control; current-advising collaboration, apparatus-site uncertainty; physical20
physicalEvidence.summary: September 2026 RAYA learns a finite-horizon recoverability predictor and bounded task-weight scheduler, which reshape constrained MPC before action selection. It runs onboard a 35g Crazyflie STM32F405 at20Hz. Forty total flights compare four controllers under fan airflow with a3g attachment or40% motor-command loss; RAYA completes10/10 missions, with floor contact in one motor-loss flight before recovery. The autonomous-car tests are simulation. CMU and Dartmouth collaborate; first author Ishaan Mahajan is currently her CMU PhD student, but the apparatus location and independent current TRIO access are unverified. Do not infer collision-free guarantees from mission completion.
